entities.summary:
Francesco Filelfo was an Italian Renaissance humanist and author of the philosophic dialogue On Exile (1456). A key figure in the Italian Renaissance, he was a humanist scholar and diplomat who played a significant role in shaping the intellectual and cultural landscape of 15th-century Europe. He was born in Mantua, Italy, and died in Venice, Italy, in 1481.

Filelfo's work had a profound impact on the development of Renaissance humanism, influencing thinkers such as Petrarch and Boccaccio. His writings on exile, politics, and literature remain important sources of insight into the intellectual currents of the time.

The legacy of Francesco Filelfo can be seen in the many scholars and writers who followed in his footsteps, including the great Renaissance statesman and philosopher, Machiavelli. Filelfo's emphasis on the importance of classical education and the pursuit of wisdom continues to resonate in contemporary debates about the role of education in society.
